rationale: I read the complete held EO 10085 original (14 FR 6617): a single paragraph rewriting section 1(d) of EO 10011 (Secretary of State powers over foreign-duty allowances), effective as of August 24, 1949. I read EO 10187, 10313 and 10391 (each restates section 1(d) of EO 10011 'as amended' in full with a new appropriation-act citation, so the 10085 wording of 1(d) is replaced in turn) and the held EO 10903 text (section 5(a) item 3: 'Executive Order No. 10085 of October 28, 1949' is hereby revoked, subject to section 5(b)). Section 5(b) preserves existing rules and regulations prescribed under the revoked provisions and actions taken under them until superseded; it is a savings clause for acts under the orders, not an independent continuing command of EO 10085, so it does not keep the order itself operative. The decisive source is the express named revocation in EO 10903; the restatement by EO 10187 is a further indication that the 10085 text of 1(d) ceased to operate earlier. I did not rely on the catalog note 'Revoked by: EO 10903' or the 1989 snapshot, which are editorial and agree. Effective date of revocation and any earlier ending remain lifecycle gaps; the gap on EO 10903 'target provision not located' is a machine matching gap only, since I read the revoking text in the held file. Provisional NO hypothesis only.
